correctness.rationale: For every finite connected loopless metric multigraph with positive edge lengths, the zero-mean Kirchhoff Laplacian L is invertible. Green duality gives evaluation f(x)=<Lf,g_x>, hence the exact squared norm ∫g_x² and norm-attaining L^{-1}g_x. The global moving-source identity g_{x_t}=(1-t)g_a+t g_b+edge_tent−ell²t(1−t)/(2T) follows from a distributional Laplacian and zero-mean uniqueness check. Squaring and elementary integration proves the exact quartic. Stationary cubic roots plus vertices (and flat edges) exhaust all maxima. Leading coefficient follows from the electric resistance identity, and Foster trace yields cycle rank−1. An independent exact-rational subdivided-graph solver checked 140 evaluations and 35 leading terms; this finite test corroborates, but does not establish, the universal claim. Boundary and normalization assumptions were independently reconstructed.

originality.rationale: The strongest inspected abstract Green result is Baker–Rumely arXiv:math/0407427, which supplies spectral inverse kernels but does not state the finite arbitrary-edge quartic of the squared inverse or norming-site classification. Solomyak and Usman address different first-order Sobolev problems. A checked previous result concerns only first-order energy. Borthwick–Jones–Harrell analyzes a diagonal heat kernel but not this polynomial envelope. The published-finding corpus comparisons found no decisive covering statement. Priority remains qualified by incompletely indexed classical spline/Green literature.
residual_risks: Classical spline/Green literature may already include an exact equivalent to the edge quartic without this terminology; no priority guarantee is claimed.

value.rationale: The natural sharp H² evaluation constant for arbitrary graph topologies and all positive edge lengths is determined by a finite exact algorithm using vertex linear systems and cubic stationary equations, with all equality functions and norming points. The algebraic degree-four envelope and its resistance/topological leading coefficient give structural information not obtainable from a single graph numerical evaluation. This is a broad motivated Sobolev/Green invariant, not an arbitrary slice, routine substitution, or known-table recalculation.
